title: Backup protocol follow-up: format and transmit complete newline-terminated headers
value: Provide a working formatted-line helper for text protocol headers, reusing the verified send-all primitive rather than duplicating a second byte-transfer loop.
why_now: Catch-up for November 15, actually reviewed and published on November 16. Sources describe their current commits, not a review performed on the missed date. A deeper review found an adjacent, explicitly stubbed contract: network_send_line must format a line and append a newline, but currently returns success without using its format or arguments. Queue this after the send-all implementation and verification packets; do not treat either as completed. Its scope is smaller and more directly connected to the existing transport priority than the numerical CLI or scheduler presentation work. It is a dependent follow-up, not a replacement for the published November 16 priority. Only source/configuration review was performed.
effort: About 1-2 hours after send-all is implemented and verified, including boundary and failure tests.
steps: Document the format-helper contract: append exactly the helper-owned newline to formatted content, define whether existing line terminators are rejected, and define null-format and formatting-failure behavior without silently modifying protocol data.

Use a measured formatting approach with vsnprintf and correct va_copy/va_end handling when traversing arguments more than once. Allocate enough space for content, newline and terminator, and check size arithmetic and allocation failure.
Send the formatted bytes and newline through network_send_all, excluding the terminating NUL. Propagate transport failures and release temporary storage on every path.

Add independent socketpair receiver tests for empty content, normal numeric/string substitution and content longer than a small stack buffer. Add controlled formatting/allocation or transport failure checks where practical; document other protocol/receive stubs as unfinished.
acceptance_checks: Receiver bytes exactly equal the formatted content followed by the documented newline, without an embedded trailing NUL or silent truncation.
Empty, ordinary and long formatted lines obey the same contract, including the documented policy for input already containing line terminators.
A peer failure returns an error through the helper, temporary storage is released on success and failure, and no second incomplete send loop is introduced.
Run focused tests and make test on a supported POSIX platform after predecessor work; do not claim the entire backup system or wire-protocol parser is complete.

evidence.observation: Reviewed November 16: src is explicitly described as implementation skeletons and stubs; the README documents reliable byte framing, Linux/macOS builds, and make test.
Reviewed November 16: network_send_all must loop until count bytes are transferred; network_send_line must format a text line and append a newline. Both return zero on success and minus one on error.
Reviewed November 16: both send functions ignore their arguments and unconditionally return zero. The file includes stdarg.h but network_send_line does not format or send anything.
Reviewed November 16: the only checks initialize recv_buf_t and assert zero length/start. No socket is created and neither send function is exercised.
Reviewed November 16: tests/test_% links common sources and lock_table.c with pthread flags; make test discovers test_*.c binaries and stops when a test returns failure.

Reviewed November 16: Ubuntu CI installs build dependencies, runs a canary check, builds with make all, then invokes make test. This is workflow configuration, not evidence that CI passed in this review.

Current source inspected November 16 converts W and unpacks its shape without explicit channel validation. Its README documents assumed-valid matrices; the separately inspected tests cover valid analytic channels, not a custom-input CLI.

Current main inspected November 16 uses Processes.txt, a fixed quantum of 10, and unconditional chart generation. The README confirms a file-driven interactive workflow, so a configurable headless runner remains useful.

alternatives.title: Build the outstanding validated custom-channel runner
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Impact: lets numerical users supply safe custom inputs. Effort: roughly 2-4 hours. Evidence is strong from the README, solver and numerical tests; however, this repeats the existing channel-runner backlog while the backup transport currently reports success without transferring data. No completion of that earlier proposal is assumed.

alternatives.title: Expose input selection and a headless metrics mode
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Impact: easier reproducible classroom runs. Effort: roughly 2-4 hours plus checking expected scheduling outputs. The entry-point limitation is confirmed, but output correctness needs further behavioral verification. The backup networking contracts give a smaller, more direct implementation and test boundary.
